74	class RagPromptPipeline:
75	    """Runs the registry-backed RAG / NER document processing pipeline."""
76	
77	    def __init__(
78	        self,
79	        *,
80	        max_ner_chunks: int = MAX_NER_CHUNKS,
81	        run_ner: bool = True,
82	        run_validation: bool = True,
83	        prefer_provider: Optional[str] = None,
84	    ):
85	        self.max_ner_chunks = max_ner_chunks
86	        self.run_ner = run_ner
87	        self.run_validation = run_validation
88	        self.prefer_provider = (prefer_provider or os.getenv(
89	            "RAG_PIPELINE_PROVIDER") or "").lower()
90	        self._openai = None
91	        self._anthropic = None
92	        self._init_clients()
93	
94	    def _init_clients(self) -> None:
95	        openai_key = os.environ.get("OPENAI_API_KEY")
96	        anthropic_key = os.environ.get("ANTHROPIC_API_KEY")
97	        if openai_key:
98	            try:
99	                from openai import OpenAI
100	
101	                self._openai = OpenAI(api_key=openai_key)
102	            except Exception as exc:  # pragma: no cover
103	                logger.warning("OpenAI client unavailable: %s", exc)
104	        if anthropic_key:
105	            try:
106	                from anthropic import Anthropic
107	
108	                self._anthropic = Anthropic(api_key=anthropic_key)
109	            except Exception as exc:  # pragma: no cover
110	                logger.warning("Anthropic client unavailable: %s", exc)
111	
112	    def _truncate(self, text: str) -> str:
113	        if len(text) <= MAX_SOURCE_CHARS:
114	            return text
115	        return text[:MAX_SOURCE_CHARS] + "\n\n[TRUNCATED_FOR_PIPELINE]"
116	
117	    def _call_llm(
118	        self,
119	        system_prompt: str,
120	        user_content: str,
121	        *,
122	        temperature: float = 0.1,
123	        max_tokens: int = 1200,
124	    ) -> str:
125	        providers = []
126	        if self.prefer_provider == "openai":
127	            providers = ["openai", "anthropic"]
128	        elif self.prefer_provider == "anthropic":
129	            providers = ["anthropic", "openai"]
130	        else:
131	            # Prefer Anthropic for structured extraction when available (matches ContentAnalysisEngine)
132	            providers = ["anthropic", "openai"]
133	
134	        last_error: Optional[Exception] = None
135	        for provider in providers:
136	            try:
137	                if provider == "anthropic" and self._anthropic:
138	                    message = self._anthropic.messages.create(
139	                        model=os.getenv(
140	                            "RAG_PIPELINE_ANTHROPIC_MODEL", "claude-3-5-sonnet-20241022"),
141	                        max_tokens=max_tokens,
142	                        temperature=temperature,
143	                        system=system_prompt,
144	                        messages=[{"role": "user", "content": user_content}],
145	                    )
146	                    return message.content[0].text
147	                if provider == "openai" and self._openai:
148	                    response = self._openai.chat.completions.create(
149	                        model=os.getenv(
150	                            "RAG_PIPELINE_OPENAI_MODEL", "gpt-4o-mini"),
151	                        temperature=temperature,
152	                        max_tokens=max_tokens,
153	                        messages=[
154	                            {"role": "system", "content": system_prompt},
155	                            {"role": "user", "content": user_content},
156	                        ],
157	                    )
158	                    return response.choices[0].message.content or ""
159	            except Exception as exc:
160	                last_error = exc
161	                logger.warning("LLM provider %s failed: %s", provider, exc)
162	
163	        if last_error:
164	            raise RuntimeError(
165	                f"All LLM providers failed: {last_error}") from last_error
166	        raise RuntimeError(
167	            "No LLM provider available. Set ANTHROPIC_API_KEY or OPENAI_API_KEY."
168	        )
169	
170	    def _run_prompt_json(
171	        self,
172	        prompt_id: str,
173	        params: Dict[str, Any],
174	        *,
175	        user_fallback: str = "",
176	    ) -> Dict[str, Any]:
177	        payload = get_prompt_with_schema(prompt_id, params)
178	        system_prompt = payload["prompt"]
179	        runtime = (payload.get("meta") or {}).get("runtime") or {}
180	        temperature = float(runtime.get("temperature", 0.1))
181	        max_tokens = int(runtime.get("max_tokens", 1200))
182	
183	        user_content = user_fallback or (
184	            "Return valid JSON only, conforming to the instructions and schema."
185	        )
186	        raw = self._call_llm(
187	            system_prompt,
188	            user_content,
189	            temperature=temperature,
190	            max_tokens=max_tokens,
191	        )
192	        parsed = _extract_json_payload(raw)
193	        if not isinstance(parsed, dict):
194	            return {"_raw_list": parsed, "_raw_text": raw}
195	        parsed["_raw_text"] = raw
196	        return parsed
197	
198	    def process(
199	        self,
200	        source_text: str,
201	        *,
202	        provenance: str = "",
203	        filename_hint: str = "",
204	        content_type_override: Optional[str] = None,
205	        skip_ner: bool = False,
206	    ) -> RagPipelineResult:
207	        result = RagPipelineResult(status="ok")
208	        result.metadata = {
209	            "provenance": provenance,
210	            "filename_hint": filename_hint,
211	            "prompts_dir": str(
212	                __import__("lib.prompt_loader", fromlist=[
213	                           "PROMPTS_DIR"]).PROMPTS_DIR
214	            ),
215	        }
216	
217	        if not source_text or not source_text.strip():
218	            result.status = "error"
219	            result.errors.append("empty source_text")
220	            return result
221	
222	        text = self._truncate(source_text.strip())
223	
224	        try:
225	            # --- Stage 1: classification ---
226	            result.prompts_used.append("document_classification")
227	            classification = self._run_prompt_json(
228	                "document_classification",
229	                {
230	                    "source_text": text,
231	                    "filename_hint": filename_hint or "",
232	                },
233	            )
234	            classification.pop("_raw_text", None)
235	            result.classification = classification
236	
237	            recommendation = str(
238	                classification.get("ingestion_recommendation") or "proceed"
239	            ).lower()
240	            content_type = content_type_override or classification.get(
241	                "content_type") or "unknown"
242	
243	            if recommendation == "reject":
244	                result.status = "rejected"
245	                return result
246	            if recommendation == "hold_for_human_review":
247	                result.status = "hold"
248	
249	            # --- Stage 2: content analysis ---
250	            result.prompts_used.append("disclosure.content_analysis")
251	            analysis = self._run_prompt_json(
252	                "disclosure.content_analysis",
253	                {
254	                    "content_type": content_type,
255	                    "context_hint": provenance or "",
256	                    "source_text": text,
257	                },
258	            )
259	            analysis.pop("_raw_text", None)
260	            result.analysis = analysis
261	
262	            # --- Stage 3: rag ingestion / chunking ---
263	            result.prompts_used.append("rag_ingestion")
264	            ingestion = self._run_prompt_json(
265	                "rag_ingestion",
266	                {
267	                    "source_text": text,
268	                    "provenance": provenance or "",
269	                    "content_type": content_type,
270	                    "target_chunk_tokens": DEFAULT_CHUNK_TOKENS,
271	                },
272	            )
273	            ingestion.pop("_raw_text", None)
274	            result.ingestion = ingestion
275	
276	            raw_chunks = ingestion.get("chunks") or []
277	            chunks: List[Dict[str, Any]] = []
278	            for chunk in raw_chunks:
279	                if not isinstance(chunk, dict):
280	                    continue
281	                body = (chunk.get("text") or "").strip()
282	                skip_reasons = chunk.get("do_not_embed_reasons") or []
283	                if not body or skip_reasons:
284	                    continue
285	                chunks.append(chunk)
286	            result.chunks = chunks
287	
288	            # --- Stage 4: NER + validation ---
289	            ner_results: List[Dict[str, Any]] = []
290	            if self.run_ner and not skip_ner:
291	                for chunk in chunks[: self.max_ner_chunks]:
292	                    chunk_id = chunk.get(
293	                        "chunk_id") or f"c{len(ner_results)+1:02d}"
294	                    heading = chunk.get("heading_path") or ""
295	                    context = " | ".join(x for x in [provenance, heading] if x)
296	                    entry: Dict[str, Any] = {"chunk_id": chunk_id}
297	
298	                    try:
299	                        result.prompts_used.append("disclosure.ner")
300	                        ner = self._run_prompt_json(
301	                            "disclosure.ner",
302	                            {
303	                                "source_text": chunk.get("text") or "",
304	                                "context_hint": context,
305	                            },
306	                        )
307	                        ner.pop("_raw_text", None)
308	                        entry["ner"] = ner
309	                    except Exception as exc:
310	                        entry["ner_error"] = str(exc)
311	                        result.errors.append(f"ner:{chunk_id}:{exc}")
312	
313	                    if self.run_validation and "ner" in entry:
314	                        try:
315	                            result.prompts_used.append("validation")
316	                            qa = self._run_prompt_json(
317	                                "validation",
318	                                {
319	                                    "target": json.dumps(entry["ner"], ensure_ascii=False),
320	                                    "source_excerpt": (chunk.get("text") or "")[:2000],
321	                                    "schema_name": "entity",
322	                                },
323	                            )
324	                            qa.pop("_raw_text", None)
325	                            entry["validation"] = qa
326	                        except Exception as exc:
327	                            entry["validation_error"] = str(exc)
328	                            result.errors.append(
329	                                f"validation:{chunk_id}:{exc}")
330	
331	                    ner_results.append(entry)
332	
333	            result.ner_results = ner_results
334	
335	            # --- Stage 5: embeddable Evidence texts ---
336	            blocked_ids = {
337	                e["chunk_id"]
338	                for e in ner_results
339	                if isinstance(e.get("validation"), dict)
340	                and e["validation"].get("safe_for_rag_index") is False
341	            }
342	            embeddable = []
343	            for chunk in chunks:
344	                cid = chunk.get("chunk_id")
345	                if cid in blocked_ids:
346	                    continue
347	                embeddable.append(chunk.get("text") or "")
348	            result.embeddable_texts = [t for t in embeddable if t.strip()]
349	
350	            # Fallback: if model returned no chunks, keep whole doc as one Evidence unit
351	            if not result.embeddable_texts and recommendation != "reject":
352	                result.embeddable_texts = [text]
353	                result.errors.append(
354	                    "ingestion_produced_no_chunks; fell_back_to_full_text")
355	
356	            index_recs = (ingestion.get("index_recommendations") or {}) if isinstance(
357	                ingestion, dict
358	            ) else {}
359	            result.metadata.update(
360	                {
361	                    "content_type": content_type,
362	                    "ingestion_recommendation": recommendation,
363	                    "priority": index_recs.get("priority"),
364	                    "chunk_count": len(result.chunks),
365	                    "embeddable_count": len(result.embeddable_texts),
366	                    "ner_chunk_count": len(result.ner_results),
367	                    "prompts_used": sorted(set(result.prompts_used)),
368	                }
369	            )
370	            return result
371	
372	        except Exception as exc:
373	            logger.exception("RAG prompt pipeline failed")
374	            result.status = "error"
375	            result.errors.append(str(exc))
376	            return result
377	
378	
379	def process_document_for_rag(
380	    source_text: str,
381	    *,
382	    provenance: str = "",
383	    filename_hint: str = "",
384	    content_type_override: Optional[str] = None,
385	    skip_ner: bool = False,
386	    **pipeline_kwargs: Any,
387	) -> Dict[str, Any]:
388	    """Convenience entry point returning a plain dict."""
389	    pipeline = RagPromptPipeline(**pipeline_kwargs)
390	    return pipeline.process(
391	        source_text,
392	        provenance=provenance,
393	        filename_hint=filename_hint,
394	        content_type_override=content_type_override,
395	        skip_ner=skip_ner,
396	    ).to_dict()

# RagPromptPipeline

**Last Updated:** 2026-07-19T00:55:00-05:00  
**Status:** Wired into disclosure-rag processing  
**Location:** `apps/disclosure-rag/processing/rag_prompt_pipeline.py`

---

## Purpose

Connect the `packages/ai/prompts` registry (RAG / NER / document-processing templates) to live disclosure-rag ingestion paths so documents are classified, chunked as Evidence, entity-extracted, and validated before indexing.

---

## Architecture

```
source text
  → document_classification
  → disclosure.content_analysis
  → rag_ingestion                 (Evidence chunks)
  → disclosure.ner (per chunk)
  → validation
  → embeddable_texts              (safe_for_rag_index only)
```

Prompt resolution: `lib/prompt_loader.py` → `packages/ai/prompts` (not the removed `packages/prompts` path).

---

## Key Modules

| Module | Role |
|--------|------|
| `rag_prompt_pipeline.py` | Orchestrator + LLM JSON calls |
| `content_analysis.py` | `process_for_rag()` / `analyze_content_with_rag_pipeline()` |
| `web_content_processor.py` | Attaches `rag_pipeline` + `embeddable_texts` on URL process |
| `lib/knowledge_base_service.py` | Writes `*_rag_pipeline.json` for web ingest |
| `lib/youtube.py` | Writes YouTube `*_rag_pipeline.json` |
| `main.py` | File ingest runs pipeline before KB/upload |
| `enhanced_content_analysis.py` | Includes pipeline in comprehensive results |

---

## Data Flow

**Inputs:** `source_text`, `provenance`, optional `filename_hint` / `content_type_override`  
**Outputs (`RagPipelineResult.to_dict()`):**

- `status`: `ok` | `hold` | `rejected` | `error`
- `classification`, `analysis`, `ingestion`, `chunks`, `ner_results`
- `embeddable_texts`: Evidence-only strings for vector upload
- `metadata.prompts_used`, integrity / recommendation fields

**Env knobs:**

| Variable | Default |
|----------|---------|
| `PROMPTS_DIR` | auto → `packages/ai/prompts` |
| `RAG_PIPELINE_PROVIDER` | anthropic-then-openai |
| `RAG_PIPELINE_MAX_NER_CHUNKS` | `8` |
| `RAG_PIPELINE_MAX_SOURCE_CHARS` | `24000` |
| `RAG_PIPELINE_CHUNK_TOKENS` | `512` |
| `RAG_PIPELINE_ANTHROPIC_MODEL` | `claude-3-5-sonnet-20241022` |
| `RAG_PIPELINE_OPENAI_MODEL` | `gpt-4o-mini` |

---

## Usage

```python
from processing.rag_prompt_pipeline import process_document_for_rag
from processing.content_analysis import ContentAnalysisEngine

result = process_document_for_rag(text, provenance="https://example.com/doc")
# or
result = ContentAnalysisEngine().process_for_rag(text, provenance="file.pdf")
```

Smoke (no API keys):

```bash
cd apps/disclosure-rag
python -m pytest tests/test_rag_prompt_pipeline_wiring.py -q
```

---

## Constraints

- Never embed agent Inference (ADR-0001). Chunk bodies are source Evidence only.
- Pipeline failures are non-fatal in web/YouTube/file paths where wrapped — legacy analysis still runs.
- Wire enum `PERSONNEL` remains; prompts map KeyFigure → PERSONNEL.
---
# RagPromptPipeline — Pseudocode

**Created:** 2026-07-19T00:40:00-05:00  
**Scope:** Wire `packages/ai/prompts` RAG/NER templates into `apps/disclosure-rag` processing.

---

## Path fix

```
FUNCTION resolve_prompts_dir():
  IF env PROMPTS_DIR set → use it
  ELSE prefer packages/ai/prompts
  ELSE fallback packages/prompts (legacy)
  ELSE ascend parents looking for either
```

Update:

- `packages/ai/prompts/yaml_loader.py`
- `apps/disclosure-rag/lib/prompt_loader.py`

---

## Pipeline

```
FUNCTION process_document_for_rag(source_text, provenance, filename_hint):
  # Stage 1 — triage
  classification ← llm_json(document_classification, {
    source_text, filename_hint
  })

  IF classification.ingestion_recommendation == "reject":
    RETURN { status: "rejected", classification }

  # Stage 2 — structured content analysis
  analysis ← llm_json(disclosure.content_analysis, {
    content_type: classification.content_type,
    source_text,
    context_hint: provenance
  })

  # Stage 3 — chunk plan (Evidence only)
  ingestion ← llm_json(rag_ingestion, {
    source_text,
    provenance,
    content_type: classification.content_type,
    target_chunk_tokens: "512"
  })
  chunks ← filter(ingestion.chunks WHERE text non-empty AND NOT do_not_embed_reasons)

  # Stage 4 — NER per chunk (cap N for cost)
  entities_by_chunk ← []
  FOR chunk IN chunks[:MAX_NER_CHUNKS]:
    ner ← llm_json(disclosure.ner, {
      source_text: chunk.text,
      context_hint: provenance + chunk.heading_path
    })
    qa ← llm_json(validation, {
      target: json(ner),
      source_excerpt: chunk.text[:2000],
      schema_name: "entity"
    })
    entities_by_chunk.append({ chunk_id, ner, qa })

  # Stage 5 — index eligibility
  safe_chunks ← chunks WHERE corresponding qa.safe_for_rag_index != false
  # (if no qa, default allow with warning)

  RETURN {
    status: "ok"|"hold",
    classification,
    analysis,
    ingestion,
    chunks: safe_chunks,
    ner_results: entities_by_chunk,
    embeddable_texts: [c.text for c in safe_chunks],  # Evidence only
    metadata: provenance + priority + integrity_flags
  }
```

---

## Integration points

```
ContentAnalysisEngine.analyze_content(text):
  # keep legacy string summary for YouTube/web summary files
  ALSO expose process_for_rag(text, provenance=...) → structured dict

WebContentProcessor / KnowledgeBaseService:
  AFTER fetch content:
    result ← engine.process_for_rag(content, provenance=url)
    WRITE rag_pipeline.json next to content/summary
    IF result.status ok:
      USE result.embeddable_texts for vector upload paths when present

cocoindex_flows.get_ner_extraction_instruction:
  continues via get_prompt("disclosure.ner") after path fix
```

---

## Non-goals

- Changing embedding model / dim
- Writing agent Inference into vector stores
- Full rewrite of EnhancedContentAnalysisEngine multi-model consensus
```

Repo: /Users/liamellis/Desktop/apps/ultraterrestrial-resurrection (branch `dev`). Working dir: `apps/disclosure-rag`.

## SHARED CONSTRAINTS — five other agents are editing this repo RIGHT NOW
- **NEVER** run `git stash`, `reset`, `checkout`, `clean`, `rebase`, `add`, `commit`. A prior agent swarm's `git stash` destroyed concurrent work here.
- **Do NOT commit.** Leave changes in the working tree; the lead reviews and commits.
- **YOU OWN ONLY:** `apps/disclosure-rag/lib/knowledge_base_crud.py`. Do not edit ANY other file — another agent owns `lib/knowledge_base_service.py`, another owns `main.py`. If your fix needs one, STOP and report it.
- **Do NOT run `dy` / `main.sh` / `main.py` against a real URL** — it writes into the archive and POSTs to production via QStash.
- **Do NOT edit `packages/knowledge-base/metadata/index.json` directly** — another agent owns that data repair. You change the *code* that writes it.

## THE BUGS (confirmed statically, then reproduced live 2026-08-01)

**Bug 1 — cross-day re-ingest silently orphans files.** `_generate_id()` (`:81-83`) computes `doc_id = md5(content)[:12]` — a genuine content hash. But `create_document()` (`:133-197`) **never checks whether `doc_id` already exists** before writing. `_get_doc_path()` (`:117-131`) uses `datetime.now().strftime("%Y-%m-%d")`, so:
- Same-day re-ingest → same date folder → overwrite in place (idempotent *by accident*).
- **Different-day re-ingest → same `doc_id`, NEW date directory → the index entry is unconditionally repointed (`:174-183`), and the previous directory's files become unreachable forever, with no warning.**

Reproduced live: a video ingested 2026-07-24 was re-ingested 2026-08-01, leaving `sources/transcripts/2026-07-24/HFLBDi87888/` orphaned while `index.json` moved to the new path. The record's `created_at` was also reset, destroying the original acquisition date.

**Bug 2 — non-atomic index writes.** `_save_index()` (`:75-79`) does a truncating `open(file,'w')` + `json.dump`. A crash mid-write corrupts `index.json` entirely. There is a correct pattern already in this repo to copy: `scripts/playlist_ingestion.py:116-129` writes to a temp file then `os.replace()`. (Read it — do not edit it.)

**Bug 3 — no locking.** `grep -rn 'flock\|filelock\|Lock(' lib/ scripts/ main.py` returns nothing. Two concurrent runs race on `index.json` with a classic lost update.

**Bug 4 — tag index duplicates.** Tag-index appends (`:191-193`) aren't deduped, so re-runs append the same `doc_id` repeatedly.

## YOUR TASKS
1. **Add a read-before-write dedup guard to `create_document()`.** If `doc_id` already exists in the index: do not silently repoint. Default behavior should preserve the existing record and return it, logging clearly that the document is already present. Add an explicit `force=False` parameter for deliberate overwrite.
2. **Preserve `created_at` on re-ingest.** Even when a record is legitimately updated, the original `created_at` must survive; only `updated_at` moves. (Audit found 81/564 records already have `created_at` *after* `updated_at` from a past backfill — don't add to that.)
3. **Never orphan.** If a re-ingest would write to a different path than the existing record points at, that is the orphaning case. Handle it explicitly — at minimum refuse-and-report by default rather than silently repointing. Do not delete the old directory.
4. **Make `_save_index()` atomic**: write to a temp file in the same directory, `os.replace()` onto the target. Mirror `playlist_ingestion.py:116-129`.
5. **Add file locking** around index read-modify-write so concurrent runs can't lose updates. Prefer stdlib `fcntl.flock` (this is macOS/Linux) over adding a dependency. Keep the lock scope tight and make sure it can't deadlock or leak on exception.
6. **Dedupe the tag index appends** (`:191-193`).
7. **Persist the content hash.** `_generate_id()` computes an md5 and throws it away. Store the full hash on the record (a `content_hash` field) so future dedup, integrity checking, and archive↔DB joins are possible. Keep `doc_id` as-is — do not change the ID scheme, other systems depend on it.

## IMPORTANT CONTEXT — do not "fix" this
YouTube content deliberately uses a **different** path (`lib/knowledge_base_service.py:71-220`) that bypasses `create_document()` and keys on `video_id`, not a content hash. That is **correct**: a live test showed re-scraping the same video produces different bytes (95,001 → 95,839 in 8 days), so content-hash dedup would create a new record forever for YouTube. Your changes must not break or reroute that path — you don't own that file.

from qstash import QStash
import os
import json
from .vector import upload_to_vector_db


def add_processed_content_to_queue(metadata, summary_file, full_content_file=None):
    """
    Add processed content to the queue for further processing.
    First uploads both full content and summary to vector DB, then adds to QStash queue.

    Args:
        metadata (dict): Metadata object containing information about the content
        summary_file (str): Path to the summary file
        full_content_file (str, optional): Path to the full content file
    """
    # Convert summary file to markdown if it's not already
    if not summary_file.endswith('.md'):
        # Get the file content
        with open(summary_file, 'r', encoding='utf-8') as file:
            content = file.read()

        # Create new filename with .md extension
        md_file = os.path.splitext(summary_file)[0] + '.md'

        # Write content to new markdown file
        with open(md_file, 'w', encoding='utf-8') as file:
            file.write(content)

        # Update the summary_file variable to use the markdown file
        summary_file = md_file

    print(f"Converted summary file to markdown: {summary_file}")

    # Read the summary content
    summary_content = ""
    if os.path.exists(summary_file):
        with open(summary_file, 'r', encoding='utf-8') as file:
            summary_content = file.read()

    # Read the full content if available
    full_content = ""
    if full_content_file and os.path.exists(full_content_file):
        with open(full_content_file, 'r', encoding='utf-8') as file:
            full_content = file.read()
    else:
        # If no full content file provided, use summary as full content
        full_content = summary_content

    # Prepare the metadata_file_path (if metadata is a file path string)
    metadata_file_path = None
    if isinstance(metadata, str) and os.path.exists(metadata):
        metadata_file_path = metadata
        # If metadata is a file path, read the content
        with open(metadata, 'r', encoding='utf-8') as file:
            metadata = json.load(file)

    # First, upload both contents to vector DB
    vector_upload_result = upload_to_vector_db(
        full_content=full_content,
        summary_content=summary_content,
        metadata=metadata
    )

    # Add vector IDs to metadata if upload was successful
    if vector_upload_result["success"]:
        metadata["full_document_vector_id"] = vector_upload_result["full_document"]["vector_id"]
        metadata["summary_vector_id"] = vector_upload_result["summary"]["vector_id"]

    client = QStash(os.getenv("QSTASH_TOKEN"))

    # Then proceed with QStash queue
    response = client.message.enqueue_json(
        queue="knowledge-base-data-processing",
        url="https://www.ultraterrestrial.app/api/workflow/processing",
        body={
            "metadata": metadata,
            "metadata_file_path": metadata_file_path,
            "summary_file_path": summary_file,
            "full_content_file_path": full_content_file,
```

1	/**
2	 * Full-text + vector search over Postgres.
3	 * Replaces xata.search.all() and searchXata() with:
4	 *   1. tsvector FTS (pg_trgm similarity as tiebreaker)
5	 *   2. pgvector cosine similarity (when embedding available)
6	 *   3. Combined ranked union
7	 */
8	import { getSql } from './client'
9	import type { SearchResponse } from './types'
10	
11	// Tables that have a search_vector tsvector column
12	const FTS_TABLES = new Set([
13	  'topics', 'key_figures', 'events', 'organizations',
14	  'sightings', 'testimonies', 'documents', 'artifacts',
15	])
16	
17	// Tables that have an embedding vector(1536) column
18	const VECTOR_TABLES = new Set([
19	  'topics', 'key_figures', 'events', 'organizations',
20	  'testimonies', 'documents', 'artifacts',
21	])
22	
23	const TABLE_ALIAS: Record<string, string> = {
24	  personnel: 'key_figures',
25	  'key-figures': 'key_figures',
26	  'key_figures': 'key_figures',
27	}
28	
29	function resolveTable(name: string): string {
30	  const lower = name.toLowerCase()
31	  return TABLE_ALIAS[lower] ?? lower
32	}
33	
34	/** FTS search against a single table. Returns rows with a ts_rank score.
35	 *  `table` is constrained to the FTS_TABLES whitelist, so inlining it as an
36	 *  identifier is injection-safe; the user query is passed as a bound param. */
37	async function ftsSingle(
38	  table: string,
39	  query: string,
40	  limit: number,
41	): Promise<Record<string, unknown>[]> {
42	  const sql = getSql()
43	  if (!FTS_TABLES.has(table)) return []
44	  return sql.query(
45	    `SELECT *, ts_rank(search_vector, plainto_tsquery('english', $1)) AS _score
46	     FROM "${table}"
47	     WHERE search_vector @@ plainto_tsquery('english', $1)
48	     ORDER BY _score DESC
49	     LIMIT $2`,
50	    [query, limit],
51	  ) as Promise<Record<string, unknown>[]>
52	}
53	
54	/** trgm-based similarity search (catches partial/fuzzy matches without FTS) */
55	async function trgmSingle(
56	  table: string,
57	  query: string,
58	  limit: number,
59	): Promise<Record<string, unknown>[]> {
60	  const sql = getSql()
61	  // Find columns that are TEXT and likely to contain names/descriptions
62	  const textCols: Record<string, string[]> = {
63	    topics:        ['name', 'description', 'summary'],
64	    key_figures:   ['name', 'bio', 'role'],
65	    events:        ['name', 'title', 'description', 'summary'],
66	    organizations: ['name', 'description'],
67	    sightings:     ['comments', 'shape', 'city'],
68	    testimonies:   ['title', 'description', 'summary'],
69	    documents:     ['title', 'summary'],
70	    artifacts:     ['name', 'description'],
71	  }
72	  const cols = textCols[table]
73	  if (!cols) return []
74	
75	  // Build a similarity expression over all text columns. Column names come from
76	  // the static map above (safe to inline); the query value is bound as $1.
77	  const simExpr = cols
78	    .map(c => `similarity(coalesce("${c}"::text,''), $1)`)
79	    .join(' + ')
80	
81	  return sql.query(
82	    `SELECT *, (${simExpr}) AS _score
83	     FROM "${table}"
84	     WHERE (${simExpr}) > 0.1
85	     ORDER BY _score DESC
86	     LIMIT $2`,
87	    [query, limit],
88	  ) as Promise<Record<string, unknown>[]>
89	}
90	
91	/**
92	 * Search a single table using FTS + trgm fallback.
93	 * Returns records enriched with { xata: { score, highlight } } for backward compat.
94	 */
95	export async function searchTable(
96	  table: string,
97	  query: string,
98	  limit = 10,
99	): Promise<Record<string, unknown>[]> {
100	  if (!query?.trim()) return []
101	  const pgTable = resolveTable(table)
102	
103	  let rows: Record<string, unknown>[] = []
104	
105	  try {
106	    rows = await ftsSingle(pgTable, query, limit)
107	  } catch {
108	    // FTS failed (e.g., table has no search_vector) — fall through
109	  }
110	
111	  if (rows.length === 0) {
112	    try {
113	      rows = await trgmSingle(pgTable, query, limit)
114	    } catch {
115	      // trgm extension not available or table not in list — return empty
116	    }
117	  }
118	
119	  return rows.map(r => {
120	    const score = (r._score as number) ?? 0
121	    const { _score, ...record } = r
122	    return {
123	      ...record,
124	      xata: {
125	        score,
126	        highlight: {},
127	      },
128	      xataReasoning: {
129	        score,
130	        relevancyLevel: score > 0.5 ? 'high relevance' : score > 0.2 ? 'moderate relevance' : 'low relevance',
131	        highlightReasons: 'Full-text search match',
132	        searchTerms: query,
133	        explanation: `Postgres FTS match (score: ${score.toFixed(3)})`,
134	      },
135	    }
136	  })
137	}
138	
139	/**
140	 * Cross-table search (replaces xata.search.all with no table specified).
141	 * Searches all FTS tables and merges results ranked by score.
142	 */
143	export async function searchAll(
144	  query: string,
145	  limit = 10,
146	): Promise<Record<string, unknown>[]> {
147	  if (!query?.trim()) return []
148	
149	  const tables = [...FTS_TABLES]
150	  const results = await Promise.allSettled(
151	    tables.map(t => searchTable(t, query, Math.ceil(limit / 2)))

249	  )

263	const recordId = (rec: Record<string, unknown>): string | undefined =>
264	  (rec.id ?? rec.xata_id) as string | undefined

266	/**
267	 * Reciprocal Rank Fusion — merge N ranked result lists into one ranking that is
268	 * invariant to each list's score scale. A record's fused score is the sum over
269	 * every list of 1/(k + rank), where rank is its 0-based position in that list.
270	 * k dampens the contribution of low-ranked items; 60 is the canonical default
271	 * from the original RRF paper (Cormack et al., 2009).
272	 *
273	 * Why this and not raw-score sort: FTS ts_rank (~0–0.1) and pgvector cosine
274	 * (~0.6–1.0) are not comparable as numbers. Sorting their union by raw score
275	 * lets vector hits dominate purely by magnitude. RRF ranks by agreement of
276	 * position across signals, so a result both searches surface rises to the top.
277	 */
278	function fuseRRF(
279	  lists: Record<string, unknown>[][],
280	  limit: number,
281	  k = 60,
282	): Record<string, unknown>[] {
283	  const fused = new Map<string, { rec: Record<string, unknown>, score: number }>()
284	
285	  for (const list of lists) {
286	    list.forEach((rec, rank) => {
287	      const id = recordId(rec)
288	      if (!id) return
289	      const contribution = 1 / (k + rank)
290	      const existing = fused.get(id)
291	      if (existing) {
292	        existing.score += contribution
293	        // Prefer the variant carrying the higher native relevance score, so the
294	        // surfaced record keeps its strongest xata/xataReasoning payload.
295	        const existingNative = (existing.rec.xata as any)?.score ?? 0
296	        const recNative = (rec.xata as any)?.score ?? 0
297	        if (recNative > existingNative) existing.rec = rec
298	      } else {
299	        fused.set(id, { rec, score: contribution })
300	      }
301	    })
302	  }
303	
304	  return [...fused.values()]
305	    .sort((a, b) => b.score - a.score)
306	    .slice(0, limit)
307	    .map(({ rec, score }) => ({
308	      ...rec,
309	      _rrfScore: score,
310	    }))
311	}
312	
313	/**
314	 * searchDatabase — the disclosure-mindmap-agent + Prometheus chat search tool.
315	 * Preserves existing interface: { table, searchTerms, searchFields, limit }.
316	 * When `embedding` is provided, runs FTS and pgvector search in parallel and
317	 * fuses them with Reciprocal Rank Fusion (scale-invariant), so keyword and
318	 * semantic matches compete on rank agreement rather than raw score magnitude.
319	 */
320	export async function searchDatabase({
321	  table,
322	  searchTerms,
323	  limit = 3,
324	  embedding,
325	}: {
326	  table?: string
327	  searchTerms?: string[]
328	  searchFields?: string[]
329	  limit?: number
330	  embedding?: number[]
331	}): Promise<Record<string, unknown>[]> {
332	  if (!searchTerms?.length && !embedding?.length) return []
333	  const query = searchTerms?.join(' ') ?? ''
334	  const pgTable = table ? resolveTable(table.toLowerCase()) : undefined
335	
336	  if (!embedding?.length) {
337	    // FTS only
338	    return pgTable
339	      ? searchTable(pgTable, query, limit)
340	      : searchAll(query, limit)
341	  }
342	
343	  // Pull a deeper candidate pool from each signal than the final limit so RRF
344	  // has rank structure to fuse, then trim to `limit` after fusion.
345	  const pool = Math.max(limit * 3, 10)
346	
347	  const [ftsResults, vecResults] = await Promise.all([
348	    query
349	      ? (pgTable ? searchTable(pgTable, query, pool) : searchAll(query, pool))
350	      : Promise.resolve([] as Record<string, unknown>[]),
351	    pgTable
352	      ? vectorSearch(pgTable, embedding, pool)
353	      : vectorSearchAll(embedding, pool),
354	  ])
355	
356	  return fuseRRF([ftsResults, vecResults], limit)
357	}
358

171	
172	function parseVector(text: unknown): number[] | null {
173	  if (typeof text !== 'string' || !text.startsWith('[')) return null
174	  try {
175	    const arr = JSON.parse(text) as number[]
176	    return Array.isArray(arr) && arr.length ? arr : null
177	  } catch {
178	    return null
179	  }
180	}
181	
182	function cosine(a: number[], b: number[]): number {
183	  let dot = 0, na = 0, nb = 0
184	  const n = Math.min(a.length, b.length)
185	  for (let i = 0; i < n; i++) {
186	    dot += a[i] * b[i]
187	    na += a[i] * a[i]
188	    nb += b[i] * b[i]
189	  }
190	  const denom = Math.sqrt(na) * Math.sqrt(nb)
191	  return denom ? dot / denom : 0
192	}

280	    if (!seeds.length) return []
281

283	    const windowMs = windowYears * 365.25 * 24 * 3600 * 1000
284	    const start = new Date(Math.min(...times) - windowMs).toISOString()
285	    const end = new Date(Math.max(...times) + windowMs).toISOString()
286	
287	    const rows = (await sql.query(

289	       WHERE date >= $1::timestamptz AND date <= $2::timestamptz AND NOT (id = ANY($3))
290	       ORDER BY date ASC

292	      [start, end, excludeIds, limit],
293	    )) as Record<string, unknown>[]
294	
295	    return rows.map(row => {
296	      const t = new Date(String(row.date)).getTime()
297	      let best = seeds[0], bestDelta = Infinity
298	      for (let i = 0; i < seeds.length; i++) {
299	        const d = Math.abs(times[i] - t)
300	        if (d < bestDelta) { bestDelta = d; best = seeds[i] }
301	      }
302	      return { row, seedId: best.id, deltaYears: bestDelta / (365.25 * 24 * 3600 * 1000) }

352	  }
353	  const [joinRecordMaps, seedRecordMaps] = await Promise.all([
354	    Promise.all([...joinIdsByTable].map(async ([t, ids]) => [t, await fetchRecords(t, [...new Set(ids)])] as const)),
355	    Promise.all([...seedsByTable].map(async ([t, ids]) => [t, await fetchRecords(t, ids)] as const)),
356	  ])
357	  const joinRecords = new Map(joinRecordMaps)
358	  const seedTitles = new Map<string, string>()
359	  for (const [t, m] of seedRecordMaps) for (const [id, r] of m) seedTitles.set(id, titleOf(t, r))
360	
361	  const out: RelatedSuggestion[] = []
362	  const taken = new Set<string>(exclude)
363	
364	  // 1) documented connections — strongest signal, always first
365	  for (const h of joinHits) {
366	    if (taken.has(h.targetId)) continue
367	    const rec = joinRecords.get(h.targetTable)?.get(h.targetId)
368	    if (!rec) continue
369	    taken.add(h.targetId)
370	    out.push({
371	      id: h.targetId,
372	      table: h.targetTable,
373	      title: titleOf(h.targetTable, rec),
374	      snippet: snippetOf(rec),
375	      score: 0.95,
376	      reason: 'connected',
377	      reasonDetail: `${h.via} — “${seedTitles.get(h.seedId) ?? h.seedId}”`,
378	      seedId: h.seedId,
379	      seedTitle: seedTitles.get(h.seedId) ?? h.seedId,
380	      record: rec,
381	    })
382	  }
383	
384	  // 2) semantic neighbors of the canvas centroid
385	  for (const n of neighbors.sort((a, b) => b.score - a.score)) {
386	    const id = String(n.row.id)
387	    if (taken.has(id)) continue
388	    taken.add(id)
389	    out.push({
390	      id,
391	      table: n.table,
392	      title: titleOf(n.table, n.row),
393	      snippet: snippetOf(n.row),
394	      score: n.score,
395	      reason: 'similar',
396	      reasonDetail: `${Math.round(n.score * 100)}% semantic affinity with “${seedTitles.get(n.seedId) ?? n.seedId}”`,
397	      seedId: n.seedId,
398	      seedTitle: seedTitles.get(n.seedId) ?? n.seedId,
399	      record: n.row,
400	    })
401	  }
402	
403	  // 3) temporal cluster around seed events
404	  for (const t of temporal) {
405	    const id = String(t.row.id)
406	    if (taken.has(id)) continue
407	    taken.add(id)
408	    const years = t.deltaYears < 1
409	      ? 'within a year'
410	      : `${t.deltaYears.toFixed(0)} year${t.deltaYears >= 1.5 ? 's' : ''} apart`
411	    out.push({
412	      id,
413	      table: 'events',
414	      title: titleOf('events', t.row),
415	      snippet: snippetOf(t.row),
416	      score: Math.max(0.2, 1 - t.deltaYears / 10),
417	      reason: 'temporal',
418	      reasonDetail: `occurred ${years} from “${seedTitles.get(t.seedId) ?? t.seedId}”`,
419	      seedId: t.seedId,
420	      seedTitle: seedTitles.get(t.seedId) ?? t.seedId,
421	      record: t.row,
422	    })
423	  }
424	
425	  // Dedupe by display title too — the events table contains near-duplicate
426	  // rows (same incident ingested twice with different ids).
427	  const seenTitles = new Set<string>()
428	  const unique = out.filter(s => {
429	    const key = `${s.table}:${s.title.toLowerCase()}`
430	    if (seenTitles.has(key)) return false
431	    seenTitles.add(key)
432	    return true
433	  })
434	
435	  // Reason diversity: raw scores are not comparable across signals (cosine
436	  // ~0.4–0.7 vs temporal ~0.7–0.9), so allocate slots per reason instead of
437	  // sorting the union — half documented connections, a quarter each for
438	  // semantic and temporal, then backfill whatever is left.
439	  const byReason = (r: RelatedReason) =>
440	    unique.filter(s => s.reason === r).sort((a, b) => b.score - a.score)
441	  const picked = [
442	    ...byReason('connected').slice(0, Math.max(3, Math.floor(limit / 2))),
443	    ...byReason('similar').slice(0, Math.max(2, Math.floor(limit / 4))),
444	    ...byReason('temporal').slice(0, Math.max(2, Math.floor(limit / 4))),
445	  ]
446	  if (picked.length < limit) {
447	    const pickedIds = new Set(picked.map(s => s.id))
448	    picked.push(...unique.filter(s => !pickedIds.has(s.id)).slice(0, limit - picked.length))
449	  }
450	  return picked.slice(0, limit)
451	}
452

@cocoindex.flow_def(name="UFOResearch")
def ufo_research_flow(flow_builder: cocoindex.FlowBuilder, data_scope: cocoindex.DataScope):
    """CocoIndex flow for UFO/UAP research documents"""

    # Add a data source to read files from knowledge base directory
    knowledge_base_path = os.getenv(
        "KNOWLEDGE_BASE_DIRECTORY_PATH", "data/documents")

    data_scope["documents"] = flow_builder.add_source(
        cocoindex.sources.LocalFile(path=knowledge_base_path,
                                    file_extensions=[".txt", ".md", ".pdf"])
    )

    # Add a collector for document embeddings
    doc_embeddings = data_scope.add_collector()

```python
def process_for_rag(
    self,
    content_text: str,
    *,
    provenance: str = "",
    filename_hint: str = "",
    content_type_override: Optional[str] = None,
    skip_ner: bool = False,
    run_ner: bool = True,
) -> Dict[str, Any]:
    """Run the registry-backed RAG/NER document pipeline. Returns structured
    classification, analysis, Evidence chunks, NER, and embeddable_texts
    suitable for vector indexing (Inference excluded)."""
    pipeline = RagPromptPipeline(run_ner=run_ner)
    return pipeline.process(
        content_text,
        provenance=provenance,
        filename_hint=filename_hint,
        content_type_override=content_type_override,
        skip_ner=skip_ner,
    ).to_dict()

def analyze_content_with_rag_pipeline(
    self,
    content_text: str,
    *,
    provenance: str = "",
    filename_hint: str = "",
    include_legacy_summary: bool = True,
    skip_ner: bool = False,
) -> Dict[str, Any]:
    """Legacy narrative summary + structured RAG pipeline artifact."""
    rag = self.process_for_rag(content_text, provenance=provenance,
                                filename_hint=filename_hint, skip_ner=skip_ner)
    legacy = self.analyze_content(content_text) if include_legacy_summary else None
    return {"legacy_analysis": legacy, "rag_pipeline": rag,
            "embeddable_texts": rag.get("embeddable_texts") or [], "status": rag.get("status")}
```

  if (!url) throw new Error('DATABASE_URL is not set')
  return url
}

import 'dotenv/config'
import { neon } from '@neondatabase/serverless'

const sql = neon(process.env.DATABASE_URL as string)

async function main() {
  const dupes = await sql`
    SELECT document, chunk_index, COUNT(*) AS n
    FROM document_chunks
    WHERE document IS NOT NULL AND chunk_index IS NOT NULL
    GROUP BY document, chunk_index
    HAVING COUNT(*) > 1
    ORDER BY n DESC
    LIMIT 20
  `
  const nullCount = await sql`
    SELECT COUNT(*) AS n FROM document_chunks WHERE document IS NULL OR chunk_index IS NULL
  `
  const total = await sql`SELECT COUNT(*) AS n FROM document_chunks`
  const dupeGroups = dupes.length

    nullDocumentOrChunkIndex: nullCount[0].n,
    duplicateGroups: dupeGroups,
    duplicateRowsTotal: dupeRowsTotal,
    sampleDuplicates: dupes.slice(0, 10),
  }, null, 2))
}

main().catch(e => { console.error(e); process.exit(1) })

11	# Agent inferences are excluded from all retrieval, search, and suggestion pathways
12	
13	The `agent_inferences` table stores the analytical layer — reasoning strings, evidentiary-state labels, and edge rationale produced by the mindmap agent. It is write-only from the product's perspective: it is never queried by `searchDatabase`, never fed into pgvector similarity searches, and never used as a source for the deterministic suggestion engine (`related.ts`).
14	
15	The alternative — making inferences retrievable — was considered and rejected. Inferences are semantically rich (they contain entity names, event references, and analytical language), so they would surface in search results and similarity queries alongside primary source material. This would silently bootstrap model output into the evidence base: a future query could retrieve an inference as if it were a sourced fact, and subsequent synthesis could treat that inference as grounding for a new inference, compounding hallucination without any visible seam. The whole epistemics of the product rest on the distinction between sourced evidence and analytical overlay; making inferences retrievable erases that distinction at the data layer where it is hardest to recover.
16	
17	The deterministic data floor must remain the floor. LLM output amplifies; it does not seed.
18	
19	## Consequences
20	
21	- `insertAgentInference` is the only write path for agent output into the database.
22	- Any new retrieval or suggestion feature must explicitly exclude `agent_inferences` from its query scope.
23	- If a future feature needs to query inferences (e.g. an adversarial Skeptic pass reviewing past syntheses), it must do so in a clearly separated read path that never mingles inference rows with entity rows in a single result set.
24

33	  'document-chunks': 'document_chunks',

35	
36	function resolveTable(name: string): string {
37	  const lower = name.toLowerCase()
38	  return TABLE_ALIAS[lower] ?? lower
39	}

41	/** FTS search against a single table. Returns rows with a ts_rank score.
42	 *  `table` is constrained to the FTS_TABLES whitelist, so inlining it as an
43	 *  identifier is injection-safe; the user query is passed as a bound param. */
44	async function ftsSingle(
45	  table: string,
46	  query: string,
47	  limit: number,
48	): Promise<Record<string, unknown>[]> {
49	  const sql = getSql()
50	  if (!FTS_TABLES.has(table)) return []
51	  return sql.query(
52	    `SELECT *, ts_rank(search_vector, plainto_tsquery('english', $1)) AS _score
53	     FROM "${table}"
54	     WHERE search_vector @@ plainto_tsquery('english', $1)
55	     ORDER BY _score DESC
56	     LIMIT $2`,
57	    [query, limit],
58	  ) as Promise<Record<string, unknown>[]>
59	}

62	async function trgmSingle(
63	  table: string,
64	  query: string,
65	  limit: number,
66	): Promise<Record<string, unknown>[]> {
67	  const sql = getSql()
68	  // Find columns that are TEXT and likely to contain names/descriptions
69	  const textCols: Record<string, string[]> = {
70	    topics:        ['name', 'description', 'summary'],
71	    key_figures:   ['name', 'bio', 'role'],
72	    events:        ['name', 'title', 'description', 'summary'],
73	    organizations: ['name', 'description'],
74	    sightings:     ['comments', 'shape', 'city'],
75	    testimonies:   ['title', 'description', 'summary'],
76	    documents:     ['title', 'summary'],
77	    artifacts:     ['name', 'description'],
78	    // No search_vector on this table (see FTS_TABLES comment above), so trgm
79	    // is the only keyword-search path in. content is the whole chunk, not a
80	    // short field like the entity tables' name/title — trgm similarity degrades
81	    // on long strings, but it's still a reachability win over zero keyword access.
82	    document_chunks: ['content'],
83	  }
84	  const cols = textCols[table]
85	  if (!cols) return []
86	
87	  // Build a similarity expression over all text columns. Column names come from
88	  // the static map above (safe to inline); the query value is bound as $1.
89	  const simExpr = cols
90	    .map(c => `similarity(coalesce("${c}"::text,''), $1)`)
91	    .join(' + ')
92	
93	  return sql.query(
94	    `SELECT *, (${simExpr}) AS _score
95	     FROM "${table}"
96	     WHERE (${simExpr}) > 0.1
97	     ORDER BY _score DESC
98	     LIMIT $2`,
99	    [query, limit],
100	  ) as Promise<Record<string, unknown>[]>

buckets = collections.Counter()
for k,g in gaps:
    if g > 1000000: buckets['>1e6 sec (~11+ days)'] += 1
    elif g > 60: buckets['>60 sec'] += 1
    elif g > 1: buckets['1-60 sec'] += 1
    elif g > 0.001: buckets['1ms-1s'] += 1
    else: buckets['<1ms'] += 1
print("\nbuckets:", dict(buckets))
EOF

"""
Throwaway verification for the knowledge_base_crud.py dedup/atomic/lock fixes.
NOT part of the repo. Uses a temp KB root — never touches the real archive.

import sys
import json
import shutil
import tempfile
from pathlib import Path
from unittest import mock
from datetime import datetime, timedelta

REPO = Path("/Users/liamellis/Desktop/apps/ultraterrestrial-resurrection/apps/disclosure-rag")
sys.path.insert(0, str(REPO))

from lib.knowledge_base_crud import KnowledgeBaseCRUD  # noqa: E402

tmp_root = Path(tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix="kb_crud_test_"))
kb_root = tmp_root / "knowledge-base"
print(f"Using temp KB root: {kb_root}")

failures = []


def check(label, cond):
    status = "PASS" if cond else "FAIL"
    print(f"[{status}] {label}")
    if not cond:
        failures.append(label)


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 1. create -> re-create same content, same day: should be a no-op, no orphan
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
crud = KnowledgeBaseCRUD(kb_path=str(kb_root))

content = "Test transcript content for HFLBDi87888 — identical bytes."
doc1 = crud.create_document(
    title="HFLBDi87888",
    content=content,
    source="https://youtube.com/watch?v=HFLBDi87888",
    doc_type="transcript",
    tags=["ufo", "testimony"],
)
path1 = crud.index["documents"][doc1.id]["path"]
print(f"First create -> doc_id={doc1.id} path={path1}")

doc2 = crud.create_document(
    title="HFLBDi87888",
    content=content,
    source="https://youtube.com/watch?v=HFLBDi87888",
    doc_type="transcript",
    tags=["ufo", "testimony"],
)
path2 = crud.index["documents"][doc2.id]["path"]

check("same-day re-create returns identical doc_id", doc1.id == doc2.id)
check("same-day re-create keeps same path (no drift)", path1 == path2)
check("same-day re-create preserves created_at", doc1.created_at == doc2.created_at)
check("only one directory exists for this doc", len(list(Path(path1).parent.parent.glob("*"))) == 1)

# tag index should not have duplicate doc_id entries after 2 creates
tag_docs = crud.index["tags"].get("ufo", [])
check("tag index deduped after re-create", tag_docs.count(doc1.id) == 1)

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 2. re-create simulating a DIFFERENT day (the orphaning bug) -> must refuse
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
future = datetime.now() + timedelta(days=8)


class FakeDatetime(datetime):
    @classmethod
    def now(cls, tz=None):
        return future


with mock.patch("lib.knowledge_base_crud.datetime", FakeDatetime):
    doc3 = crud.create_document(
        title="HFLBDi87888",
        content=content,  # identical bytes -> identical doc_id
        source="https://youtube.com/watch?v=HFLBDi87888",
        doc_type="transcript",
        tags=["ufo", "testimony"],
    )

path3 = crud.index["documents"][doc3.id]["path"]

check("cross-day re-ingest keeps same doc_id", doc3.id == doc1.id)
check("cross-day re-ingest does NOT repoint the index", path3 == path1)
check("cross-day re-ingest preserves original created_at", doc3.created_at == doc1.created_at)
check(
    "original directory still exists and was not orphaned",
    Path(path1).exists() and (Path(path1) / "metadata.json").exists(),
)
# The would-be new (future-dated) directory must NOT have been created.
future_date_folder = future.strftime("%Y-%m-%d")
future_dir = crud.transcripts_path / future_date_folder
check(
    "no new future-dated directory was created for the refused re-ingest",
    not future_dir.exists(),
)

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 3. force=True same-day overwrite: allowed, in place, created_at preserved
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
doc4 = crud.create_document(
    title="HFLBDi87888",
    content=content,
    source="https://youtube.com/watch?v=HFLBDi87888",
    doc_type="transcript",
    tags=["ufo", "testimony"],
    force=True,
)
check("force=True overwrite keeps same doc_id/path", doc4.id == doc1.id)
check("force=True overwrite still preserves created_at", doc4.created_at == doc1.created_at)
check("force=True overwrite bumps updated_at", doc4.updated_at != doc1.updated_at)

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 4. content_hash persisted on the record and in the index
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
check("Document.content_hash populated", len(doc1.content_hash) == 32)
check(
    "index entry carries content_hash",
    crud.index["documents"][doc1.id].get("content_hash") == doc1.content_hash,
)

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 5. index.json is valid JSON after all the above (atomic writes held up)
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
with open(crud.index_file) as f:
    on_disk = json.load(f)
check("index.json parses as valid JSON after all writes", doc1.id in on_disk["documents"])
check("no leftover .tmp file after writes", not (crud.metadata_path / "index.json.tmp").exists())

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 6. update_document preserves created_at, refreshes content_hash
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
updated = crud.update_document(doc1.id, content="different content now")
check("update_document preserves created_at", updated.created_at == doc1.created_at)
check(
    "update_document refreshes content_hash",
    updated.content_hash == crud._content_hash("different content now"),
)

shutil.rmtree(tmp_root, ignore_errors=True)

print()
if failures:
    print(f"{len(failures)} CHECK(S) FAILED:")
    for f_ in failures:
        print(f"  - {f_}")
    sys.exit(1)
else:
    print("ALL CHECKS PASSED")

-- =============================================================================
-- 0002_ann_indexes.sql  —  Vector ANN indexes + document_chunks integrity
-- Target: any managed Postgres 16+ with pgvector (Neon, current host). Host-portable.
-- Created: 2026-08-01
-- Why deferred from 0001: 0001_init.sql:22-26 explicitly reserved ANN index
-- creation for this migration, to run AFTER the embedding backfill (SP#2).
-- That backfill is now done — all 10 vector(1536) columns are either fully
-- populated or empty — so the indexes below can be created safely.
--
-- Conventions:
--   • HNSW, not IVFFlat — matches 0001's own stated reasoning: HNSW needs no
--     build-time data (unlike IVFFlat, whose list centroids are computed from
--     whatever rows exist at CREATE INDEX time) and handles incremental
--     inserts without a rebuild. Both properties matter here: mindmaps (0
--     rows) and summary_files (1 row, NULL embedding) are effectively empty
--     today but will grow.
--   • vector_cosine_ops — every cosine-similarity query in this codebase
--     (search.ts, related.ts) uses the <=> operator; the opclass must match.
--   • CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY IF NOT EXISTS — safe to re-run, and does not
--     hold a lock that blocks reads/writes on tables that already carry
--     production traffic (topics, key_figures, events, ..., document_chunks).
--
-- ⚠️  CRITICAL — DO NOT WRAP THIS FILE IN A TRANSACTION.
-- CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY cannot run inside a transaction block (Postgres
-- will reject it with "CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY cannot run inside a
-- transaction block"). Unlike 0001_init.sql, this file deliberately has NO
-- BEGIN/COMMIT wrapper and NO \set ON_ERROR_STOP-driven single-shot execution
-- via a transactional runner. Apply it with a plain psql invocation, e.g.:
--     psql "$DATABASE_URL" -f migrations/rebuild/0002_ann_indexes.sql
-- Each CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY statement commits its own catalog change as
-- it goes; if one statement fails partway through (e.g. after a crash), the
-- IF NOT EXISTS + CONCURRENTLY combination on re-run will either skip the
-- already-built index or clean up and retry safely. If a CONCURRENTLY build
-- is ever interrupted, check for an INVALID index (`\d <table>` shows
-- "INVALID") and DROP INDEX CONCURRENTLY it before re-running this file.
--
-- THIS MIGRATION HAS NOT BEEN APPLIED. It is authored for review; the lead
-- decides when/how it runs against the live database.
-- =============================================================================

-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- document_chunks integrity check (read-only, informational)
-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- Before adding UNIQUE(document, chunk_index) below, verify no partial-retry
-- duplicates exist. Verified 2026-08-01 against live data: 4,946/4,946 rows
-- have non-NULL (document, chunk_index), 0 duplicate groups. Re-run this
-- SELECT before applying if more ingestion has happened since:
--
--   SELECT document, chunk_index, COUNT(*) AS n
--   FROM document_chunks
--   WHERE document IS NOT NULL AND chunk_index IS NOT NULL
--   GROUP BY document, chunk_index
--   HAVING COUNT(*) > 1
--   ORDER BY n DESC;
--
-- If that query returns any rows when this is actually applied, STOP —
-- the ADD CONSTRAINT below will fail loudly (Postgres refuses to add a
-- UNIQUE constraint over data that violates it), which is the correct
-- fail-closed behavior. Do not delete rows to force it through without
-- understanding which retry produced the duplicate.

-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- document_chunks: UNIQUE(document, chunk_index)
-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- document_chunks currently has only a random-UUID PK (0001_init.sql:467-476)
-- and no constraint preventing a partial ingest retry from re-inserting the
-- same (document, chunk_index) pair as a new row. ALTER TABLE ... ADD
-- CONSTRAINT takes a lock and validates existing data in one pass — there is
-- no CONCURRENTLY form for UNIQUE constraints, but this table is 4,946 rows
-- (small) so a brief validation scan is acceptable; unlike the CREATE INDEX

-- trivial and harmless — the index just starts empty and grows as rows are
-- inserted/backfilled, so there's no reason to special-case or skip them;
-- doing so would only mean remembering to add the index later.

CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY IF NOT EXISTS idx_topics_embedding
    ON topics USING hnsw (embedding vector_cosine_ops);

    ON key_figures USING hnsw (embedding vector_cosine_ops);

    ON testimonies USING hnsw (embedding vector_cosine_ops);

CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY IF NOT EXISTS idx_documents_embedding
    ON documents USING hnsw (embedding vector_cosine_ops);

CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY IF NOT EXISTS idx_artifacts_embedding
    ON artifacts USING hnsw (embedding vector_cosine_ops);

CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY IF NOT EXISTS idx_document_chunks_embedding
    ON document_chunks USING hnsw (embedding vector_cosine_ops);

-- Empty today (0 rows) — see comment above on why it's still created now.
CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY IF NOT EXISTS idx_mindmaps_embedding
    ON mindmaps USING hnsw (embedding vector_cosine_ops);

CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY IF NOT EXISTS idx_summary_files_embedding
    ON summary_files USING hnsw (embedding vector_cosine_ops);

All 7 fixes are complete in `apps/disclosure-rag/lib/knowledge_base_crud.py`, verified with a 19/19-passing throwaway test against a temp KB root, and reported to team-lead. Summary:

1. **Dedup guard in `create_document`** (new `force: bool = False` param) — same-day re-ingest is now an explicit no-op by default; cross-day re-ingest (the orphaning bug) is refused unconditionally regardless of `force`, leaving the original files and index entry untouched.
2. **`created_at` preserved** on force-overwrite and on `update_document` (verified already correct there, made lock-safe).
3. **Never orphan** — path-drift case always refused and logged, never silently repointed.
4. **`_save_index()` made atomic** — temp file + `os.replace()`, mirroring `scripts/playlist_ingestion.py`.
5. **File locking** — new `_locked_index()` contextmanager using `fcntl.flock` on a dedicated `index.json.lock`, wrapping the full read-modify-write cycle in `create_document`/`update_document`/`delete_document`, with a reload-under-lock so concurrent instances don't lose updates. Noted one residual gap I couldn't fix: `knowledge_base_service.py` (owned by another agent) calls `_save_index()` directly, bypassing the lock.
6. **Tag index deduped** in both `create_document` and `update_document`.
7. **`content_hash` persisted** — new `Document.content_hash` field (default `""` for backward compat with old records), `doc_id` derivation unchanged.

The YouTube ingest path in `lib/knowledge_base_service.py` was not touched and remains keyed on `video_id`, bypassing `create_document()` entirely, so it's unaffected by the dedup logic.

```sql
-- =============================================================================
-- 0002_ann_indexes.sql  —  Vector ANN indexes + document_chunks integrity
-- Target: any managed Postgres 16+ with pgvector (Neon, current host). Host-portable.
-- Created: 2026-08-01
-- Why deferred from 0001: 0001_init.sql:22-26 explicitly reserved ANN index
-- creation for this migration, to run AFTER the embedding backfill (SP#2).
-- That backfill is now done — all 10 vector(1536) columns are either fully
-- populated or empty — so the indexes below can be created safely.
--
-- Conventions:
--   • HNSW, not IVFFlat — matches 0001's own stated reasoning: HNSW needs no
--     build-time data (unlike IVFFlat, whose list centroids are computed from
--     whatever rows exist at CREATE INDEX time) and handles incremental
--     inserts without a rebuild. Both properties matter here: mindmaps (0
--     rows) and summary_files (1 row, NULL embedding) are effectively empty
--     today but will grow.
--   • vector_cosine_ops — every cosine-similarity query in this codebase
--     (search.ts, related.ts) uses the <=> operator; the opclass must match.
--   • CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY IF NOT EXISTS — safe to re-run, and does not
--     hold a lock that blocks reads/writes on tables that already carry
--     production traffic (topics, key_figures, events, ..., document_chunks).
--
-- ⚠️  CRITICAL — DO NOT WRAP THIS FILE IN A TRANSACTION.
-- CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY cannot run inside a transaction block (Postgres
-- will reject it with "CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY cannot run inside a
-- transaction block"). Unlike 0001_init.sql, this file deliberately has NO
-- BEGIN/COMMIT wrapper. Apply it with a plain psql invocation, e.g.:
--     psql "$DATABASE_URL" -f migrations/rebuild/0002_ann_indexes.sql
-- \set ON_ERROR_STOP on below makes psql abort the whole file on the first
-- failing statement instead of printing an error and silently continuing —
-- without it, a failed ALTER TABLE (e.g. from the 0/4,946-nulls assumption
-- below going stale) would not stop the rest of the file from "succeeding".
-- Each CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY statement commits its own catalog change as
-- it goes; if one is ever interrupted mid-build, check for an INVALID index
-- (`\d <table>` shows "INVALID") and DROP INDEX CONCURRENTLY it before
-- re-running this file — re-running while it's INVALID will not repair it
-- because IF NOT EXISTS sees it as already there.
--
-- THIS MIGRATION HAS NOT BEEN APPLIED. It is authored for review; the lead
-- decides when/how it runs against the live database.
-- =============================================================================

\set ON_ERROR_STOP on

-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- HNSW ANN indexes — one per vector(1536) column
-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- Run first (before the document_chunks integrity fix below) because these
-- are the expensive, long-running part and carry no data risk — if the
-- integrity fix at the bottom ever needs to abort, the indexes should still
-- be left in place rather than lost to a whole-file failure.
--
-- All 10 are created, including the two effectively-empty tables (mindmaps,
-- summary_files). An HNSW build over 0 rows or all-NULL embeddings is
-- trivial and harmless — the index just starts empty and grows as rows are
-- inserted/backfilled, so there's no reason to special-case or skip them;
-- doing so would only mean remembering to add the index later.

CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY IF NOT EXISTS idx_topics_embedding
    ON topics USING hnsw (embedding vector_cosine_ops);

CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY IF NOT EXISTS idx_key_figures_embedding
    ON key_figures USING hnsw (embedding vector_cosine_ops);

CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY IF NOT EXISTS idx_events_embedding
    ON events USING hnsw (embedding vector_cosine_ops);

CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY IF NOT EXISTS idx_organizations_embedding
    ON organizations USING hnsw (embedding vector_cosine_ops);

CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY IF NOT EXISTS idx_testimonies_embedding
    ON testimonies USING hnsw (embedding vector_cosine_ops);

CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY IF NOT EXISTS idx_documents_embedding
    ON documents USING hnsw (embedding vector_cosine_ops);

CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY IF NOT EXISTS idx_artifacts_embedding
    ON artifacts USING hnsw (embedding vector_cosine_ops);

CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY IF NOT EXISTS idx_document_chunks_embedding
    ON document_chunks USING hnsw (embedding vector_cosine_ops);

-- Empty today (0 rows) — see comment above on why it's still created now.
CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY IF NOT EXISTS idx_mindmaps_embedding
    ON mindmaps USING hnsw (embedding vector_cosine_ops);

-- Empty today (1 row, NULL embedding) — see comment above on why it's still
-- created now.
CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY IF NOT EXISTS idx_summary_files_embedding
    ON summary_files USING hnsw (embedding vector_cosine_ops);

-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- document_chunks: prevent partial-retry duplicates
-- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- document_chunks currently has only a random-UUID PK (0001_init.sql:467-476)
-- and nothing stopping a partial ingest retry from re-inserting the same
-- (document, chunk_index) pair as a new row. scripts/rebuild/ingest.py always
-- supplies both values together on every INSERT (never NULL), so making them
-- NOT NULL matches how the table is actually written.
--
-- Verified 2026-08-01 against live data (read-only, before this file was
-- authored — re-run before applying if more ingestion has happened since):
--   SELECT document, chunk_index, COUNT(*) AS n
--   FROM document_chunks
--   WHERE document IS NOT NULL AND chunk_index IS NOT NULL
--   GROUP BY document, chunk_index HAVING COUNT(*) > 1;
-- Result: 4,946/4,946 rows had non-NULL (document, chunk_index); 0 duplicate
-- groups; 0 rows with either column NULL.
--
-- Why NOT NULL first: a plain UNIQUE constraint in Postgres treats NULLs as
-- distinct from each other (NULLS DISTINCT is the default), so
-- UNIQUE(document, chunk_index) alone would NOT catch a retry that inserted
-- rows with a NULL in either column — it would silently let duplicates
-- through in exactly the failure mode this constraint exists to prevent.
-- Since live data already satisfies NOT NULL on both columns, enforcing it
-- closes that gap instead of leaving a documented loophole.
ALTER TABLE document_chunks ALTER COLUMN document SET NOT NULL;
ALTER TABLE document_chunks ALTER COLUMN chunk_index SET NOT NULL;

-- Wrapped in a DO block per 0001_init.sql's own convention (see its
-- "FOREIGN KEY CONSTRAINTS" / "UNIQUE CONSTRAINTS" sections) so re-running
-- this file after a successful apply doesn't fail on duplicate_object.
DO $$ BEGIN
  ALTER TABLE document_chunks
    ADD CONSTRAINT uq_document_chunks_doc_index UNIQUE (document, chunk_index);
EXCEPTION WHEN duplicate_object THEN NULL; END $$;

-- =============================================================================
-- END 0002_ann_indexes.sql
-- =============================================================================

```text
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""
Mem0 integration helpers using modern SDK patterns
- Memory client with agent integration
- Async support for better performance
- Best-effort error handling for non-critical operations

Environment variables:
- MEM0_API_KEY (required for cloud) or NEXT_PUBLIC_MEM0_API_KEY
- MEM0_USER_ID (default: default_agent)
- MEM0_ENABLE (optional: true/false, default: enabled if API key present)
- MEM0_AGENT_ID (default: disclosure-rag-agent)
"""

import os
import logging
import asyncio
from typing import Any, Dict, List, Optional, Union
from functools import wraps

logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)

# Global variables for mem0 client
_mem0_client = None
_mem0_async_client = None


def _get_api_key() -> Optional[str]:
    """Get API key from environment variables."""
    return os.environ.get("MEM0_API_KEY") or os.environ.get("NEXT_PUBLIC_MEM0_API_KEY")


def _is_enabled() -> bool:
    """Check if mem0 integration is enabled."""
    api_key = _get_api_key()
    if not api_key:
        return False
    flag = os.getenv("MEM0_ENABLE", "").strip().lower()
    # Enabled by default if API key exists
    if flag in {"0", "false", "no", "off"}:
        return False
    return True


def _get_mem0_client():
    """Get or create mem0 client instance."""
    global _mem0_client
    
    if not _is_enabled():
        return None
        
    if _mem0_client is None:
        try:
            from mem0 import Memory
            
            config = {
                "provider": "openai",
                "config": {
                    "model": "gpt-4o-mini",
                }
            }
            
            api_key = _get_api_key()
            if api_key:
                config["api_key"] = api_key
                
            _mem0_client = Memory(config)
            logger.info("Mem0 client initialized successfully")
        except ImportError:
            logger.warning("mem0ai package not installed; skipping mem0 integration")
            return None
        except Exception as e:
            logger.warning(f"Failed to initialize mem0 client: {e}")
            return None
    
    return _mem0_client


async def _get_mem0_async_client():
    """Get or create async mem0 client instance."""

def add_web_article_memory(title: str, url: str, content: str, summary: Optional[str] = None, 
                          tags: Optional[List[str]] = None, user_id: Optional[str] = None) -> None:
    """Add web article content to mem0 memory using modern SDK patterns."""
    if not _is_enabled():
        return
    
    metadata = {
        "type": "web_article",
        "source": "disclosure-rag",
        "url": url,
        "tags": tags or [],
        "title": title,
    }
    
    # Use summary if available, otherwise use content excerpt
    text_content = summary or content[:2000]
    messages = [
        {"role": "system", "content": "Processing web article for UAP/UFO research"},
        {"role": "user", "content": f"Web article analysis: '{title}'\n\nContent: {text_content}"}
    ]
    
    add_memory(messages, user_id=user_id, metadata=metadata)

	path: string;

	type: string;
}

	title: string;
	doc_type: "transcript" | "article" | "case_file" | string;

	path: string;
	date_folder?: string;
	created_at: string;
	updated_at: string;
	tags: string[];
	source?: string;
	youtube_id?: string;
	uses_original_structure?: boolean;

		file_size?: number;
		file_type?: string;
		[key: string]: unknown;
	};
}

export interface KnowledgeBaseIndex {
	documents: Record<string, KnowledgeBaseDocument>;
	/** Tag name -> document IDs carrying that tag. */
	tags: Record<string, string[]>;
	last_updated: string;
}

Report sent to team-lead. Summary of what was delivered:

**`packages/db/src/postgres/search.ts`** — added `document_chunks` to `VECTOR_TABLES`, added a trgm keyword-fallback (`content` column) since it has no `search_vector`, and special-cased `vectorSearch` to `LEFT JOIN documents` so chunk results carry `document_title`/`document_url`/`document_source_tier` for attribution. No changes to the existing RRF fusion, FTS, or entity-table logic.

**`packages/db/src/postgres/related.ts`** — left untouched by design: `document_chunks` isn't a canvas-addable entity type, has no title handling, and would surface noisy near-duplicate fragments where the parent `documents` row is already the right granularity. The perf problem flagged there (`related.ts:232-239` full seq scan) is resolved anyway once migration 0002 lands, since all 7 tables it scans get HNSW indexes.

**`packages/db/migrations/rebuild/0002_ann_indexes.sql`** (new, not applied) — HNSW indexes on all 10 `vector(1536)` columns, plus `NOT NULL` + `UNIQUE(document, chunk_index)` on `document_chunks` (verified 0 duplicates and 0 nulls in live data first; `ingest.py` always supplies both values, so `NOT NULL` matches actual write behavior — this also closes a gap a bare `UNIQUE` would have missed, since Postgres treats NULLs as distinct by default). File has `\set ON_ERROR_STOP on`, no transaction wrapper (required for `CONCURRENTLY`), and idempotent constraint addition matching `0001`'s `DO $$...EXCEPTION` style.

Typecheck: 357 pre-existing errors, all in dead Xata-era type files, none touching the two files I edited. Only read-only SELECTs were run against the live database.

def add_web_article_memory(title: str, url: str, content: str, summary: Optional[str] = None, 
                          tags: Optional[List[str]] = None, user_id: Optional[str] = None) -> None:
    """Add web article content to mem0 memory using modern SDK patterns."""
    if not _is_enabled():
        return
    
    metadata = {
        "type": "web_article",
        "source": "disclosure-rag",
        "url": url,
        "tags": tags or [],
        "title": title,
    }
    
    # Use summary if available, otherwise use content excerpt
    text_content = summary or content[:2000]
    messages = [
        {"role": "system", "content": "Processing web article for UAP/UFO research"},
        {"role": "user", "content": f"Web article analysis: '{title}'\n\nContent: {text_content}"}
    ]
    
    add_memory(messages, user_id=user_id, metadata=metadata)

## 1. search.ts diff (file:line references are post-edit)

- **`FTS_TABLES`** (search.ts:15-18): unchanged. document_chunks has no `search_vector` column so it can't join this set.
- **`VECTOR_TABLES`** (search.ts:24-27): added `'document_chunks'`. This is what makes the 4,946 embedded chunks reachable via `vectorSearch`, `vectorSearchAll`, and `searchDatabase` — previously they had zero readers repo-wide except the Python `ingest.py` write path.
